rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is sparse, so the first experiment should explore a balanced multimodal configuration with diverse components. This experiment tests a multimodal setup using PCA for RNA, ViT for images, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion. It clarifies the potential of combining these components, which is critical for understanding interactions between modalities. Starting with a well-rounded configuration provides foundational insights to guide subsequent choices.

The existing evidence shows config_001 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000 RNA, vit_l image, avgpool, weighted) achieved 0.635 accuracy. This experiment tests changing the RNA encoder to scvi_n200 and image encoder to resnet50 while keeping aggregation and fusion methods consistent. This clarifies whether these key component changes improve performance, balancing exploration of encoder alternatives with exploitation of prior aggregation/fusion success.

Existing evidence shows config_005 (multimodal, scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) achieves 0.6776 accuracy. This experiment tests replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation (config_013), which could improve performance by capturing more complex interactions. It directly builds on the promising RNA/image encoder combination from config_005 while exploring a key design choice (aggregation method) that remains untested.

Existing evidence shows config_013 (scvi_n200 RNA, resnet50 image, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests whether replacing the image encoder with imagenet_vit_l (a stronger pre-trained model) while keeping other components the same could further improve performance. It clarifies the impact of the image encoder choice, a key design decision, without deviating too far from the current promising direction.

The existing evidence shows that using transformer aggregation and imagenet_vit_l image encoder (as in config_049) yields high accuracy. This experiment tests whether switching to concat fusion while keeping the same RNA encoder (pca_n2000) and image encoder could improve performance, clarifying the impact of fusion methods. It balances exploration of critical design choices (fusion) while building on the strong foundation of the current best configuration.

Existing evidence shows config_049 (scvi_n200 RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy (0.725). This experiment tests the same RNA/image encoders but with avgpool aggregation instead of transformer, clarifying whether aggregation method significantly impacts performance. It balances exploitation of proven components with exploration of a critical design choice, maximizing potential for improving accuracy within remaining experiments.

The existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 with imagenet_vit_l and transformer aggregation/weighted fusion (config_049) achieves the highest accuracy. This experiment tests scgpt RNA encoder with the same image encoder and fusion settings to determine if the RNA encoder choice is critical. It clarifies whether alternative encoders can match or exceed current performance while maintaining consistency in other components, balancing exploitation of proven components with exploration of RNA encoder variations.

The existing evidence shows config_049 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted) achieves the highest accuracy (0.725). Testing config_018 (pca_n2000 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted) clarifies whether the RNA encoder choice (scvi_n200 vs pca_n2000) impacts performance. This experiment reduces uncertainty about the optimal RNA encoder while maintaining the high-performing image encoder and aggregation method. It balances exploitation (building on successful components) and exploration (testing a key design choice).

The existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, and transformer aggregation with weighted fusion achieves the highest accuracy (0.724989). This experiment tests the same RNA and image encoders with transformer aggregation but uses concat fusion instead. This clarifies whether the fusion method (weighted vs concat) is critical for performance, while leveraging the strong foundation of scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l. It balances exploration of fusion methods with exploitation of proven components.

The existing evidence shows that configurations using transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_049 with 0.725 accuracy) perform best. This experiment tests pca_n2000 RNA encoder with resnet50 image encoder, maintaining transformer aggregation and weighted fusion, which could validate if combining different encoders with the top-performing architecture improves accuracy further.
